heard: An explosion shown 20 times brighter than our entire Milky Way galaxy. In June 2015, twin automated telescopes located in chilly discovered Assassin 15LH blazing brilliantly across the dark night sky. The incredible event reached a peak brightness 570 billion times greater than our sun. Located roughly 3.8 billion light years away, its strange spectrum completely lacked hydrogen and helium lines. Unlike typical blasts in small dwarf galaxies, this mysterious explosion erupted inside a massive galaxy. Astronomers actively debate whether it was powered by a fast-spinning magnetar or a supermassive black hole. That is why an explosion shone 20 times brighter than our entire Milky Way galaxy.
